as_told: Van Halen's tour contract demanded a bowl of M&Ms backstage with all the brown ones removed. It was not vanity: it was a test, so if David Lee Roth found brown M&Ms, he knew the promoter had not read the contract carefully and the whole stage setup had to be checked.
lesson: A small, easy-to-check detail placed inside detailed instructions shows whether the reader actually read and followed them.
what_happened: Van Halen's 1982 tour rider, 53 typewritten pages, lists under 'Munchies' 'M&M's (WARNING: ABSOLUTELY NO BROWN ONES)'. David Lee Roth's memoir Crazy from the Heat (1997) gives the purpose in his own words: it was 'just as a little test' in the technical part of the rider; if he saw a brown M&M he would line-check the whole production, because the promoter had not read the contract. The earliest telling found, Gordon Matthews' 1984 band biography, tells the brown-M&M story from the 1980 tour. In the 1982 rider the clause is on page 40, under food requirements; Roth's memoir places the test 'in the technical aspect of the rider'. The saved rider page does not show it among the technical requirements.

lesson_verdict.why: An instructional manipulation check, an instruction hidden in a survey that a careful reader must follow, finds a large share of participants who did not read; and those who fail it also fail to follow other instructions, so the small check predicts wider carelessness.

confidence_note: The rider clause rests on The Smoking Gun's reproduction of the 1982 rider (images viewed; quote taken from the page text). Roth's memoir was read only as Open Library snippets. The story of damage at the 1980 Pueblo show, and its cost, was not checked against 1980 records, which are not online; it does not affect the class or the lesson. Retellings say the clause was hidden among technical requirements; the 1982 rider page saved has it under food requirements, and only Roth's memoir links it to the technical part of the rider.
